questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most potent androgen?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dihydrotestosterone is the most potent androgen. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 834

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.solutionHtml:
Aromatase (CYP19) converts testosterone to estradiol. Certain effects of testosterone are mediated by estradiol. 

In men with deficient CYP19 or ER receptors, the epiphyses do not fuse, the long bones grow indefinitely and such patients are osteoporotic. Administration of estradiol can correct the bone abnormalities in CYP19 deficiency. However, this cannot be used in those with ER receptor defects.  

Testosterone is converted to dihydrotestosterone (DHT) by 5-alpha-reductase.

Androstanedione and epiandrosterone are metabolites of DHT due to the action of 17-beta-HSD.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 835

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: A 59-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer is started on flutamide therapy. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Flutamide acts by competitive inhibition of androgen receptors and is used to treat prostate cancer.

Flutamide is a non-steroidal antiandrogen that competes with androgens such as testosterone and dihydrotestosterone for binding to the androgen receptors in the prostate gland. By doing so, it prevents them from stimulating the prostate cancer cells to grow.

In addition to its use in prostate cancer, flutamide has been used to treat hyperandrogenism (excess androgen levels) in women, such as in those with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and Hirsutism.

Other anti-androgens are:

  • Bicalutamide, apalutamide, and nilutamide
  • Spironolactone  (aldosterone antagonist with antiandrogen activity)
  • Cyproterone acetate (progestin with antiandrogen activity)
  • Cimetidine (H2 blocker with anti-androgen activity)

Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators (SARMs) are a class of androgen receptor ligands that have similar anabolic properties to anabolic steroids, but with reduced androgenic side effects. There are no FDA-approved SARMs at present.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 839

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: A 25-year-old medical student is worried about his receding hairline and is thinking about taking finasteride. The drug enhances hair growth by acting on which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Finasteride is a competitive inhibitor of 5 α-reductase enzyme and thereby inhibits the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone.

Finasteride selectively inhibits the Type 2 isoenzyme of 5α-reductase. It is indicated for use in:

  • Benign prostatic hyperplasia 
  • Male pattern baldness
  • Hirsutism.




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 840

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: Which of the following inhibits spermatogenesis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gossypol is a non-steroidal agent that inhibits spermatogenesis.

Gossypol is obtained from cottonseed. It inhibits spermatogenesis by exerting toxic effects on seminiferous tubules but has low efficacy. Libido and potency are not significantly affected and fertility usually returns after a few months of discontinuation of the drug. But, around 10% of the patients may remain infertile. Hypokalemia is a major adverse effect and may even lead to transient paralysis.

Low efficacy and significant toxicity have caused gossypol to be abandoned as a candidate male contraceptive. 





Journal, Contraception; httpkats://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0010782402002949
Katzung Basic and clinical pharmacology 13th edition, Page No.745

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: A 30-year-old male patient presented to the urology OPD with complaints of erectile dysfunction and was prescribed a PDE-5 inhibitor. Identify the drug.
questions.solutionHtml:
Tadalafil is a PDE-5 inhibitor used in the treatment of patients with erectile dysfunction.

Penile erection is mediated by NO and cGMP. During arousal, the corpus cavernosum produces nitric oxide which in turn stimulates the formation of cGMP. This leads to relaxation of the smooth muscle of corpus cavernosum and penile arteries, causing engorgement of corpus cavernosum producing an erection. The biological actions of cGMP are terminated by phosphodiesterase enzymes and PDE-5 is the major cGMP metabolizing enzyme in the penile tissue.

Phosphodiesterase-5-inhibitors include:

  • Sildenafil
  • Tadalafil - Longest acting (24-36 hrs), bioavailability is not affected by food 
  • Vardenafil
  • Avanafil - Most Rapid-acting (within 15 -30 mins) 

Option A: Podofilox topical cream is used in the treatment of genital warts and molluscum contagiosum lesions.

Option B: Finasteride is a 5 α-reductase inhibitor.

Option C: Apalutamide is a androgen receptor antagonist.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 840

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: A 40-year-old diabetic patient was prescribed sildenafil for his erectile dysfunction. Following this, he develops a blurring of vision and complains that things seem to appear with a bluish-green hue. Inhibition of which of the following enzymes is likely to have caused his visual side effects?
questions.solutionHtml:
Visual disturbance seen with sildenafil is due to PDE-6 inhibition.

Sildenafil is used for the treatment of erectile dysfunction principally due to its inhibitory actions on PDE-5 (Phosphodiesterase 5) in the vascular tissues of the corpus cavernosa. However, it also exerts minor inhibitory action against PDE-6, which is present exclusively in rod and cone photoreceptors and results in blurring and blue-green tinting of vision.

Tadalafil and avanafil have better PDE-5/PDE-6 selectivity, compared to sildenafil and vardenafil and hence have lesser visual side effects.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no: 612,700

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: Which of the following is a prostaglandin that can be administered as an intracavernosal injection for erectile dysfunction?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alprostadil can be given as a direct intracavernosal injection for erectile dysfunction.

Alprostadil is a natural PGE1 preparation. It is usually used in patients who are not responding to PDE-5 inhibitors. It is also available as an intraurethral suppository.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 683

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: A 35-year-old physician presented to the ED with a prolonged painful erection induced by intracorporeal injection of an alprostadil+phentolamine combination. He had been using this technique to overcome occasional performance anxiety. Corporeal aspiration reveals dark coloured blood and based on further workup, a diagnosis of low flow priapism is made. Which of the following is the drug of choice to treat his condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phenylephrine is the drug of choice for the treatment of low flow priapism. 

Characteristics of low-flow priapism include painful rigid erection and ischemic corpora, indicated by dark blood upon corporeal aspiration. 

Prazosin, and, phenoxybenzamine are alpha-blockers that cause vasodilation and can worsen priapism.





Journal, Cent European J Urol. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3921718/
Online Resource, https://emedicine.medscape.com/article/437237-treatment#d8

questions.topic: Marrow · 52.Androgens and Drugs for Erectile Dysfunction
questions.stem: A 19-year-old male athlete seeks your opinion on the usage of anabolic steroids to improve his performance. What would be your advice?

options.label: A
options.text: Reassure the patient that all anabolic steroids are safe to use

options.label: B
options.text: Explain clearly that only newer anabolic steroids are safe to use as they have negligible androgenic action

options.label: C
options.text: Advice against use and sensitise the patient that all anabolic steroids have significant androgenic action

options.label: D
options.text: Explain that older testosterone preparations are more appropriate for use in male athletes

questions.answerText: Advice against use and sensitise the patient that all anabolic steroids have significant androgenic action
questions.solutionHtml:
All anabolic steroids have significant androgenic action and the use of anabolic steroids by athletes is not recommended.

Testosterone and its derivatives are used for their anabolic effects but they have significant androgenic action. Some of them (17 methyl derivatives) are also hepatotoxic. The current consensus is to advise against the use of such anabolic steroids.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no: 741
